channel.title: Israel National News Flashes
channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll resigns amid tensions with Hegseth
item.description: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll submits resignation to President Trump after months of reported tensions with Secretary of War Pete Hegseth.

item.title: Otzma Yehudit: Goal of Segalovitz's alliance with Mansour - a Hamas state in the Negev and Galilee
item.description:
The Otzma Yehudit party responded to former MK Yoav Segalovitz's decision to join the Ra’am party ahead of the election.
"During the first Muslim Brotherhood government, Yoav Segalovitz transferred millions of shekels from the state treasury directly to Ra’am's Hamas-affiliated organizations. In the second Muslim Brotherhood government, which they want to establish together with Eisenkot, Yair and Naftali, they will halt the demolition of homes in the Negev and dismantle the units established by Minister Ben Gvir within the Israel Police that are seriously disrupting protection rackets and polygamy. The goal of Segalovitz's alliance with Mansour is one thing: to establish a Hamas state in the Negev and Galilee. We must not give them this gift. We will not allow it," the party said.

item.title: Report in Iran: Saudi oil tanker detained in Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
Iranian media outlets reported that a Saudi oil tanker was detained in the Strait of Hormuz after attempting to transit the strait near the coast of Oman.
However, Reuters noted that there has been no Saudi confirmation of the report.

item.title: Sara Netanyahu takes a swipe: Why does the Prime Minister need to be informed?
item.description: Sara Netanyahu questions how Yair Golan reached the front lines on October 7 before her husband was briefed on the massacre. Democrats Party calls the comments "a red line."

item.title: Trump: Iran is 'totally defeated militarily', they don’t know who their leader is
item.description: President Trump says Iran is militarily defeated as US strikes resume, while stressing there is no reason to use nuclear weapons against Tehran.

item.title: The purpose of Tithes
item.description: Ma’aser Kesafim (tithing money) is the modern equivalent of the tithes, priestly gifts, and gifts to the poor that were given from the produce of the fields and from livestock and its primary purpose today is to support teachers of Torah in Israel and help the poor.

item.title: Report: Trump weighs limited US Strikes on Iran in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: US officials say CENTCOM developed plan for periodic strikes aimed at preventing Iran from rebuilding radar, air defense and anti-ship missile capabilities.

item.title: Poll: Smotrich-Feiglin alliance wins 5 seats
item.description: According to the poll, without a merger between the parties, Religious Zionism remains below the electoral threshold, while Ofer Winter’s party enters the Knesset in its place.

item.title: IDF announces new senior appointments, Bar Kalifa to head Central Command
item.description: Defense Minister Israel Katz approves sweeping IDF appointments, including Dado Bar Kalifa as Central Command chief following controversy over the nomination.

item.title: Israel launches major crackdown on illegal construction in Judea and Samaria
item.description: Israeli forces demolish illegal construction near the security fence and an ancient archaeological site in two-day enforcement operation in Area C.

item.title: Health Ministry: Suspected Ebola infection in person who returned from Congo
item.description: The Health Ministry announced Monday evening that it had received a report of another person suspected of having Ebola after returning from the Congo.

item.title: Suspect arrested over sedative-laced baby food
item.description: Police arrest a suspect over sedatives allegedly injected into Prinok baby food after three Jerusalem-area infants were hospitalized with severe symptoms.

item.title: IDF elimnates Hamas supply and maintenance commander
item.description:
Earlier today (Monday), the IDF struck in the Sabra area in Gaza City and eliminated Omar Mohammed Roshdy Saraj, a commander in the Gaza City supply and maintenance company in the Hamas terrorist organization.
As part of his role, the terrorist managed the supply of weapons to Hamas terrorists in the Gaza City area.

item.title: ‘Every Jew must feel committed’: French cousins enlist in the IDF
item.description: After making Aliyah from France, cousins Gad and Elior enlist in the IDF’s Hasmonean Brigade, driven by faith, duty and a desire to defend Israel.

item.title: Into the fray: How Bibi ruined Israel
item.description: The impressive post-October 7th achievements of the current government are often overlooked and undervalued. If you are have RLB (anyone but Bibi) virus, they are likely to be denied. Opinion.

item.title: Netanyahu hails security agreement with Greece
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated: "The security agreement signed today with Greece, one of the largest in the country's history, is a direct continuation of the Eastern Mediterranean alliance we forged a decade ago with Greece and Cyprus. It serves as further proof of the tremendous capabilities of Israel's defense and technological industries. This move expresses Israel's strength, the confidence in our defense exports, and the strengthening of regional alliances."

item.title: Nobel Prize winner Prof. Ada Yonath dies at 87
item.description: The pioneering ribosome researcher and one of Israel’s leading scientists has died after decades of research that led to the development of advanced medicines. “An extraordinary scientist."

item.title: Preventing nuclear war is an urgent obligation
item.description: A nuclear war - any nuclear war - would resemble an incurable disease. Of necessity, all meaningful “therapies" must lie in prevention. Opinion.

item.title: Broad daylight raid: Undercover officers nab terror suspect in Shechem
item.description: Undercover Border Police officers enter deep into Balata camp in broad daylight, surround a vehicle, and arrest a wanted terror suspect.

item.title: Security increased for Central Elections Committee Chairman Noam Sohlberg
item.description: Police have decided to increase security around Supreme Court Justice and Central Elections Committee Chairman Noam Sohlberg following a situation assessment and intelligence that was received.

item.title: ‘Immense fortitude’: Netanyahu honors reserve combat servicemen and women
item.description: Netanyahu meets reserve combat servicemen and women, hears their battlefield stories and joins a photo shoot for an exhibition set to tour Israel and abroad.

item.title: Draft crackdown could bring thousands of Breslov Hassidim to Meron
item.description: With draft dodgers facing obstacles to leaving Israel, Breslov organizers prepare Meron for thousands who may be unable to spend Rosh Hashanah in Uman.

item.title: Haredi yeshiva student arrested days before his son’s circumcision
item.description: A Hasidic yeshiva student was arrested at a military base in Eilat and sentenced to ten days in military prison, just days before his son’s brit milah ceremony.

item.title: Desalination plants shut down for hours due to weather conditions
item.description: Unusual weather conditions caused severe turbidity in the seawater, leading to the shutdown of desalination plants south of Hadera.

item.title: After Rabbi Yosef’s attack, Rabbi Kook’s glowing words for Rabbi Lior resurface
item.description: Following Rabbi Yitzhak Yosef’s criticism of Rabbi Dov Lior, a historic letter resurfaces revealing Rabbi Tzvi Yehuda Kook’s glowing praise for him.

item.title: Trump on Iran: 'We're going to hit them hard'
item.description:
US President Donald Trump told Fox News on Monday that the US will respond to the Iranian attack on US forces overnight in Jordan. "We're going to hit them hard; there will be a response."
The President indicated that all except for one missile were intercepted.

item.title: Trump: 'Iran is Dead'
item.description: US President calls Iran a 'failed state' that has killed over 100,00 of its own people.

item.title: 18 million shekels: Force 100 soldiers sue prosecutors, police and Channel 12
item.description: Three Force 100 soldiers seek 18 million shekels from prosecutors, law enforcement officials and media figures, alleging false arrest, leaks and defamation.
